fatal_errors: The proposed entropy-stabilized, sluggish-segregation mechanism is opposite to the observed kinetically controlled, active-diffusion mechanism.
The material system is changed from sub-10 nm equiatomic AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles to a generic CoCrFeMnNi alloy.
The intervention omits the specified in situ vacuum heating ramp and temperature-resolved STEM/EDS and molecular-dynamics analysis.
The predicted suppression of segregation directly contradicts Au/Cu surface segregation, melting or evaporation, particle loss, and size reduction.
explanation: The response addresses thermal stability of high-entropy alloys in general and supplies a nominally testable comparison, but it does not reconstruct the target system or result. Its central hypothesis invokes configurational-entropy stabilization and suppressed segregation, whereas the target finds non-sluggish Au/Cu diffusion driven by surface-energy minimization, enhanced by shape evolution, with evaporation and approximately 22% size reduction at 973 K. The generic 500–1000 °C boundary misses the important onset near 673 K and the sub-10 nm, shape-dependent regime. Comparing a high-entropy alloy with a pure metal or low-entropy alloy also changes chemistry and phase constitution, so it cannot cleanly isolate configurational entropy from elemental interactions. The absence of cited background evidence further makes the proposal unsupported rather than a well-supported alternative.
